title: n8n vs Make vs Zapier for AI automation: which fits which business
metaTitle: n8n vs Make vs Zapier for AI Automation
description: A practical comparison of n8n, Make and Zapier for AI-powered business automation: control, cost model, AI agent support and who each one suits.
author: Techlio Engineering
answer: Choose Zapier when a non-technical team needs simple automations live this week. Choose Make when the workflows branch and you want a visual builder with more control. Choose n8n when the automation is core to the business, involves AI agents or sensitive data, or will run at a volume where per-task pricing hurts, because n8n can be self-hosted and extended with code.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.text: All three connect your apps and move data between them, and all three now offer AI steps. They differ in who they are built for. Zapier is built for speed and ease. Make is built for visual, multi-branch scenarios. n8n is built for technical teams who want control over hosting, logic and cost.

sections.heading: How they compare
sections.text: These are the differences that decide most projects we scope.
bullets: Ease of use: Zapier is the simplest to start with. Make takes a few hours to learn. n8n expects someone comfortable with data structures and, sometimes, a little JavaScript or Python.
Hosting and data: Zapier and Make are cloud services. n8n can run in its cloud or on your own servers, which matters when customer or patient data must stay inside your environment.

Cost model: Zapier charges by task and Make by operation, so cost rises with every step a workflow runs. n8n charges by workflow execution in its cloud, and self-hosting replaces usage fees with server and maintenance cost.
AI agents: all three can call a language model. n8n goes further with agent nodes that hold memory, call tools and query a vector store, so a multi-step agent can live inside the workflow.
Custom logic: n8n lets you drop into code at any step and build your own nodes. Make and Zapier offer code steps with tighter limits.
Integrations: Zapier has the largest catalogue of ready-made connectors. With n8n, anything with an API can be connected through an HTTP request, at the cost of a little more setup.

sections.heading: When each one is the right choice
sections.text: Zapier suits a small team automating a handful of simple hand-offs, such as a form filling a CRM and posting to chat. Make suits operations teams with branching scenarios who want to see the whole flow on one canvas. n8n suits companies where automation is becoming infrastructure: many workflows, AI agents that read and act on company data, approval steps, audit logs, and volumes where usage pricing would outgrow the value.

sections.heading: What usually goes wrong
sections.text: The tool is rarely the reason an automation fails. The common causes are no error handling, no alert when a step breaks, credentials owned by one person, and AI steps with no check on their output. Whichever platform you pick, plan for retries, logging, a human approval step for anything unusual, and a named owner.

sections.heading: Our recommendation
sections.text: Start where your team can maintain the result. If nobody technical will own it, a well-built Zapier or Make setup beats an n8n instance nobody understands. If you expect AI agents, sensitive data or high volume within a year, start on n8n and avoid a migration later. Prices and features change often, so check each vendor's current pricing page before you decide.

faqs.question: Is n8n free?
faqs.answer: n8n's source is available and can be self-hosted without a licence fee for internal business use under its fair-code licence. You still pay for servers and for the time to maintain it. n8n also sells a hosted cloud plan.

faqs.question: Can I move from Zapier to n8n later?
faqs.answer: Yes, but workflows are rebuilt by hand because there is no automatic converter. A typical migration recreates each workflow, tests it against real data and runs both side by side for a short period.

faqs.question: Which is best for AI agents?
faqs.answer: n8n has the most complete agent tooling of the three, with memory, tool calling and vector store nodes. Zapier and Make are fine for single AI steps such as classifying or summarising a message.
